newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ICE rates Hungary's Gardenia shares as 'buy'.
newsitem.headline: ICE rates Hungary's Gardenia shares as 'buy'.

text.p: Hungary's leading curtain factory has substantial growth prospects, London-based ICE Securities said in a company report, rating the stocks a 'buy'.

"We forecast significant growth prospects for Gardenia and given its undemanding prospective multiples compared with highly rated home improvement companies on the Budapest bourse, our recommendation is an unqualified buy," ICE's analysts said.

Analysts Rudi Voros and Gerhard Auer said that the two most important target markets with significant further potentials were Croatia and Slovakia, where currently no soft-furnishing manufacturing capicity existed.
They added that they expected Gardenia to gradually increase its presence elsewhere in the central and eastern European region.
"Through acquisitions and organic growth we expect the company to increase its regional market share significantly over the forecast period," the analysts said.

The company has begun a combined capital market transaction which includes the sale of 222,000 own shares and the issue of 400,000 new shares during a subscription period between March 10 and 21. The money the company raises will be spent on new investments and acquisition.
Voros and Auer said the company will benefit from a recovery of the Hungarian economy this year, too.
"This is a well-timed strategy, since it will coincide with a recovering domestic economy and with positive developments within the housing repair and construction markets," they said.
For 1997 Hungary targets Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth of up to three percent amid the revival of investments and consumption. In 1996 the rate of growth was seen flat.
The analysts said that on the level of new orders the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism forecasts a 2-3 percent growth in output of the construction industry.
In 1997 ICE expects Gardenia to post an unconsolidated 516 million forints of net profit after 303 million in 1996 and 440 million in 1995.

The subscription price of Gardenia's shares, which have 500 forints face value, was set at 1,465 forints or $8.30. The company has already received a go-ahead from the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) council to list its shares provided it fulfils certain technical conditions.
